name: Wren Building at William and Mary
dates: Weekdays and Saturdays, student tours on a schedule
customer: Architecture people, prospective students, history buffs
unique: The oldest academic building in continuous use in the United States, begun in 1695 and rebuilt twice after fires, with the original chapel, the Great Hall and a courtyard where the college's students drilled before marching off to war.
buzz: Student guides from the Spotswood Society tell the fire and rebuilding story better than any plaque. Free, and the quietest hour in a town built on tourism.

name: Muscarelle Museum of Art
customer: Art students, drawing crowds, rainy day visitors
unique: A university museum with a small permanent collection and a habit of landing old master drawings and prints that belong in a much bigger city, mounted in a building on the William and Mary campus.
buzz: Exhibitions rotate often and the shows are ambitious for the space. Free admission makes it an easy hour between historic area tickets.

name: The Cheese Shop
customer: Locals on lunch break, tourists, picnic packers
unique: A Merchants Square shop that has sold cheese, wine and its own house dressing since the early 1970s, with a sandwich counter in the back that working Williamsburg orders from and a bread end basket by the register.
buzz: The house dressing and the sandwich line are the whole review. Locals avoid it at noon in summer and go at two.

name: Williamsburg Farmers Market
unique: A Saturday market in Merchants Square with produce, oysters, cheese, baked goods and plants from farms within a couple of hours, set among restored 18th century buildings and busy enough that the whole square smells like coffee and bread.
buzz: Small but well curated, and locals treat it as the real town underneath the historic area. The oyster and baked goods stands sell out early.

name: Busch Gardens Williamsburg
dates: March–early January, Christmas Town in winter
unique: A theme park built as a set of European hamlets in a wooded ravine, with eight coasters including a launched wing coaster and a wooden coaster that regularly ranks among the best in the world, plus a show schedule and a beer hall.
buzz: Coaster people come for the lineup and stay for the landscaping, which is the thing everyone mentions. Summer crowds and parking prices are the complaints.

name: Water Country USA
unique: Virginia's largest water park, with a wave pool, a lazy river and a set of slides that includes a four person raft run and a bowl ride, in a park small enough to cover in a day without a plan.
buzz: People rate it as the best water park within a few hours of Richmond and warn about chair claims and locker lines. Go on a weekday in June.

name: Historic Jamestowne
company: National Park Service and Preservation Virginia
unique: The actual site of the 1607 fort, where archaeologists are still digging and have found the bones and artifacts of the first English settlement, with a memorial church, a museum of the findings and a walk along the James where the first ships tied up.
buzz: Seeing the excavation in progress is what separates it from the recreated settlement next door. Rangers and archaeologists explain the ongoing work, and the church tower is the oldest standing structure on the site.

name: Jamestown-Scotland Ferry
unique: A free state run car ferry that crosses the James River on a twenty minute ride between Jamestown and Surry, running around the clock since the 1920s and carrying anyone who shows up, no ticket and no reservation.
buzz: Locals use it as a shortcut and visitors use it as a boat ride that costs nothing. Dolphins and bald eagles are a common sight from the deck.

name: Williamsburg Winery at Wessex Hundred
unique: A winery on a 300 acre farm with a stone cellar built into the hillside, growing vinifera grapes in tidewater heat and running tours that end in a tasting room looking out over the vineyard.
buzz: The reserve tasting and the cellar tour are the draw, and the restaurant is a destination on its own. Reviews note the pours are generous and the property is prettier than the wines.

name: American Revolution Museum at Yorktown
unique: A museum of the whole Revolution told from the bottom up, with a gallery of period weapons and documents, an outdoor Continental Army encampment and a farm where interpreters fire muskets and cook over open fires, on the ground where the war ended.
buzz: The encampment artillery demonstrations are what people remember, and the exhibits on enslaved and Native people are treated seriously. It is a state museum that behaves like a national one.

name: Watermen's Museum
customer: Boat people, families, Chesapeake history fans
unique: A small museum on the Yorktown waterfront about the people who made a living from the bay: skipjack models, crab pots, oyster tongs, decoys and tools, with working watermen often on hand to explain what each one did.
buzz: Volunteers who actually worked the water are the reason to go, and the view from the back deck over the York is free with admission. Fifteen minutes if you skim, an hour if you talk.

name: York River State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A tidewater park on the York with a beach where Miocene whale bones and shark teeth wash out of the cliff, boat rentals on Taskinas Creek, and trails through marsh and hardwood that are flat enough for small kids.
buzz: Fossil hunting is the draw and rangers will tell you what you found. The creek paddle at high tide is the other reason people come back.

name: Yorktown Market Days
dates: Saturday mornings, April–December, plus themed markets
unique: A Saturday market on the Riverwalk Landing beach at the bottom of the Yorktown bluff, with produce, seafood, baked goods and food trucks, and a view of the York River that makes people stay longer than they planned.
buzz: The setting is the review. Themed markets through the year, including a maritime festival and a harvest market, draw bigger crowds than the regular Saturdays.

name: Colonial Parkway
unique: A twenty three mile divided parkway with no commercial traffic, brick bridges and stone walls that links Jamestown, Williamsburg and Yorktown along the James and York rivers, built in the 1930s to look like a colonial road.
buzz: People drive it without realizing it is a national park unit. Cyclists treat the whole length as a training route and the river overlooks are the pull-offs worth stopping at.

name: Chrysler Museum of Art
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with a strong European and American collection, an entire wing of glass from ancient to studio, and a working glass studio where you can watch a piece being blown or book a session to make one.
buzz: Free admission for a collection this size is the thing visitors cannot get over. The glass studio demonstrations and the Tiffany window are the usual favorites.

name: Norfolk Botanical Garden
unique: Virginia's largest botanical garden, with more than sixty themed gardens, a tram ride through the whole property, a butterfly house in season and a bog full of carnivorous plants, on land first planted by Works Progress Administration crews in the 1930s.
buzz: The tram is worth the ticket for anyone with limited walking and the rose garden in May is the local photo spot. The butterfly house is the kid draw.

name: Norfolk Tides at Harbor Park
unique: Triple A baseball on the Elizabeth River with the downtown skyline behind the outfield, cheap tickets, a crab cake stand and a promenade where you can watch the game standing at a rail with a boat going by.
buzz: The ballpark is the reason people go even when the team is bad. Tickets are cheap, the food is local and the waterfront seats are the ones to ask for.

name: Attucks Theatre
customer: Music fans, history people, community events
unique: A 1919 theater built and financed by Black businessowners in the Huntersville neighborhood, part of the chitlin circuit that booked Duke Ellington and Cab Calloway, restored in 2004 and still running concerts and plays under its original name.
buzz: The restoration is beautiful and the sightlines from the balcony are good. Locals talk about the history as much as the shows.

name: Virginia Zoo
customer: Families with young kids, animal people
unique: A zoo that has been operating since 1900 on land beside the Lafayette River, with an African trail, a tiger exhibit and a farmyard, small enough to finish in an afternoon and old enough to have generations of Norfolk families in its membership rolls.
buzz: Parents call it the right size for small kids and praise the train and the splash area. It is not a destination zoo, and nobody claims otherwise.

name: Cape Henry Lighthouse
unique: The first lighthouse authorized by the federal government, finished in 1792 and still standing on the beach where the first English settlers landed, with a spiral stair you climb to a gallery looking straight down the Atlantic and into Chesapeake Bay.
buzz: The climb is 191 steps and the view from the top is the reason. The older tower leans slightly, which people notice on the way up.

name: First Landing State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: Twenty miles of trails through bald cypress swamp and maritime forest, a beach on the bay, and campground cabins built by the CCC in the 1930s, on the shore where the Jamestown colonists first came ashore.
buzz: The cypress swamp trail is unlike anything else in the state and the bay beach is calm enough for small children. Summer parking fills early.

name: Virginia Aquarium and Marine Science Center
customer: Families, marine biology students, rainy day crowds
unique: A aquarium with a walk through tunnel under a 300,000 gallon tank, a river otter habitat and a stranding response team that rescues whales and sea turtles on the Virginia coast, with the rescue work explained rather than hidden.
buzz: The otters and the tunnel are the kid favorites and the staff talks about rehabilitation cases by name. Tickets are expensive enough that people look for the combination deals.

name: Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge
dates: Daily, daylight, some areas closed in winter for waterfowl
unique: Nine thousand acres of marsh, dunes and barrier beach at the southern end of Virginia Beach, where the road ends and the wild beach begins, with a paddle trail through the back bay and a winter population of snow geese and tundra swans.
buzz: Birders come for the migration and paddlers for the quiet water. The walk down the beach to False Cape is a full day and there is no shade.
